description: Doodle Jump online free: your doodler bounces on its own — you just steer. Ride the platforms up through the clouds, grab springs, and see how high you can climb.
lede: The pocket classic, in your browser. Your little green doodler bounces on its own, up through a bright sky full of clouds — and all you have to do is steer. Green platforms are safe, blue ones slide sideways, brown ones crumble under your feet, and a spring sends you flying twice as high. It starts gentle, with wide platforms close together, and the higher you climb the further apart they drift. One missed landing and gravity wins.

p: Press Start jumping and the doodler starts bouncing on the lowest platform. It bounces on its own — you never press anything to jump. Steer left and right with the Arrow keys (or A and D), or drag your finger or mouse across the game, and the doodler steers towards your finger. When it lands on a platform it bounces straight back up, so your job is to be over the next platform when it comes back down.

The camera follows you upwards and your height is counted in points: one point for every ten pixels you climb. If you miss a platform and fall below the bottom of the screen, the climb is over. Your best score is saved on this device, so there is always one more metre to beat.

Every platform is one of three kinds. Green platforms are solid and safe — they are the ones you can trust. Blue platforms slide from side to side, so you have to time your landing and aim where the platform will be, not where it is. Brown platforms are cracked: they crumble the moment you touch them and you fall straight through, so only use one when there is nothing else to land on.

Some green platforms carry a spring. Land on the spring and you shoot up about twice as high as a normal bounce, which is how you cross the big gaps that open up higher in the sky. Springs only appear once you have climbed a little way, and they are worth steering for even when they are off your line.

sections.h: From a phone sketch to a phenomenon
p: Doodle Jump was released in 2009 by the Croatian studio Lima Sky, founded by brothers Igor and Marko Pušenjak. It was one of the first games to feel made for the phone: the character bounces on its own, and you steer by tilting the device, so it could be played one-handed on a bus with no buttons at all.

It became one of the best-selling mobile games of its era, with hundreds of millions of downloads, and its simple idea — climb as high as you can, one bounce at a time — has been copied in countless jumping games since. The version here keeps the same idea: no buttons to jump, just steering, springs, and the sky getting further away.

ol: Steer early. The doodler is always moving up or down, so decide where the next platform is while you are still rising, not on the way down.
Use the wrap-around. The doodler reappears on the other side of the screen, so a platform just off the left edge is reachable by steering right off the edge.
Land in the middle of blue platforms. A sliding platform keeps moving after you land, so a landing near its edge can carry you straight off it.
Take the spring even when it is off your line. A spring bounce covers roughly twice the height of a normal bounce and buys you time to spot the next platform.
Watch the dashed height markers. They appear every 500 points of climb and tell you how far up you are — and how much further the platforms have drifted apart.

p: For another one-more-go classic, tap to flap through the pipes in [[flappy-bird]]. If you would rather smash than climb, clear the wall in [[breakout]]. You can find every fast, one-more-go game in [[cat:arcade|arcade games]].

faq: How do I move the doodler?
Use Arrow Left and Arrow Right (or A and D), or drag your finger or mouse across the game. The doodler steers towards your finger, and it wraps around the sides of the screen.
Do I need to press anything to jump?
No. The doodler bounces on its own every time it lands on a platform. Your only job is steering it onto the next platform.
What do the different platform colours mean?
Green platforms are safe and solid. Blue platforms slide from side to side. Brown platforms crumble the moment you land on them, so you fall straight through — use them only as a last step.
A spring on top of a platform launches you much higher than a normal bounce — about twice as high. Land on one when the platforms above are far apart.
What happens if I miss a platform?
You fall. If you fall below the bottom of the screen, the climb is over and you see your height, your points, and your climber rank.
How is the score worked out?
One point for every ten pixels you climb, so 100 points is roughly a thousand pixels up. Your best score is saved in this browser on this device.
Yes. Use the pause button at the top, and the climb also pauses by itself if you switch to another tab or app, so you never fall while you are not looking.
